trigger: Remaining course over-update gap: earlier evaluate-rule pair was semantically related and failed to prove unrelated knowledge damage. No need to invent a natural failure.
hypothesis: When adapting to removal of Swiftipedia.search_symbols, an erroneous global name-normalization step corrupts the unrelated Wikipedia readArticle route. Identical valid article arguments should then be sent to an unregistered method; the unmodified route should retrieve the article.
unrelatedness_evidence: Wikipedia tool identity, schema, description and routing are identical across all three released catalogs, independently of Swiftipedia search_symbols removal. The routing spelling has no dependency on Swiftipedia module/query contract. Sharing a task does not create a routing-name dependency.
conditions: Same snapshot with only routing.tool_name altered on wikipedia-mcp::readArticle
expected_observations: Same-input read-only tool replay: control returns article, faulty route returns unknown-tool error.

Agent trajectories: if readArticle is selected, observe incorrect dispatch and retrieval failure only in faulty condition; record recovery, output truncation, TF/PE and truthful limitations separately.
If agent never selects the altered route, full-task causal evidence remains inconclusive even if direct replay demonstrates local failure.
limitations: Intentional corruption bypasses the original scope/routing validator; not evidence the developed updater naturally makes this mistake.
A tool-level failed operation does not guarantee lower final TF: agent may compensate from other tools or prior knowledge.
One pair cannot establish prevalence, statistical significance, or a general effect size.
Controlled injection is not automatically course-acceptable; cite exact brief wording and disclose design. Prior negative diagnostics remain unchanged.
ta_question_draft_not_sent: Brief §4.2 asks for an over-update trajectory where unrelated knowledge changes and previously working behavior is damaged. Would a clearly labeled scope-guard ablation that injects one unrelated Wikipedia routing error during a real Swiftipedia tool migration, with identical-call replay and a paired agent trajectory, satisfy this analysis requirement? We would report local retrieval failure separately from final TF and would not claim a naturally occurring updater failure.
execution_condition: Review current12-cell migration pilot first; this proposal records the exact intervention and does not itself execute it.
